hero.headline: St. Lucie County school employee arrested for lewd acts in front of two girls
hero.teaser: A St. Lucie County public school employee faces charges for lewd and lascivious behavior in front of two children.
hero.body:
A St. Lucie County school employee was arrested for lewd and lascivious acts committed in front of two sisters aged 14 and 11. Police documents detail allegations that the employee was touching himself in front of the two children.

The arrest follows an investigation into the inappropriate behavior. The suspect worked in the St. Lucie County public school system.

The employee faces charges of lewd and lascivious acts. Authorities have not disclosed which school the employee worked at or their specific role in the district.

The investigation into the incident remains ongoing. No additional information about the circumstances surrounding the alleged acts has been released by authorities.

cards.headline: Four arrested after holding gun to teen's head and pushing him from car
cards.teaser: Four people were arrested after allegedly holding a gun to a Florida teenager's head and forcing him out of a vehicle.
cards.body:
Four individuals were arrested after deputies say they held a gun to a Florida teen's head and pushed him out of a moving car. The incident involved multiple suspects who allegedly threatened the teenager with a firearm.

Deputies responded to the case and identified four suspects involved in the violent incident. The teen was forced from the vehicle after being threatened at gunpoint.

All four suspects were taken into custody and face charges related to the armed assault and kidnapping. The investigation determined the sequence of events that led to the teen being pushed from the car.

cards.headline: Florida fentanyl summit draws teens, grieving parents and DEA chief as overdose crisis takes center stage in Orlando
cards.body:
Teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country joined grieving parents and federal law enforcement at the Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week, united by a shared mission to stop fentanyl before it kills more Americans. The summit drew students who traveled from around the country to learn about the resurgence of fentanyl so they can return home with a message about one of the country's deadliest drug threats. Hannah Kahn, 18, explained that a relative addicted to methamphetamine encouraged her to prevent similar destruction in others' lives. Jasmine Figueroa, 19, told adults that drug education should not be a taboo topic, saying young people will get educated one way or another and parents should be the first to tell them the truth about drugs.

This year's summit welcomed the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration as a partner. DEA Administrator Terrance Cole spent time with victim families and said the poison is being manufactured and distributed out of Mexico by the Mexican cartels. Cole said the president has designated the Mexican cartels as foreign terrorists, which opens different avenues for the DEA to target them. The students, who are members of their community anti-drug coalitions, said fentanyl spreads because it is often laced in other drugs and young people may not recognize the danger. Kahn said people are not seeking out fentanyl necessarily, but it is just within other drugs.

For parents who have lost children, the summit is deeply personal. Mari Rodriguez's daughter, Imam, died of fentanyl poisoning in 2023 after she made the mistake of buying a Percocet pill that had fentanyl in it. Rodriguez said every day she has to live with what she didn't know and questions why she gave her some space. She said the fight against fentanyl in the U.S. should have started in 2009, when the first fentanyl was found on streets, because the people behind it are not stopping. A DEA chemist recently told reporters that one sample turned out to be 16 percent fentanyl, which is high.

While deaths from the synthetic opioid are down, tracking how widespread fentanyl has become is nearly impossible in part because of Narcan, an over-the-counter nasal spray that is increasing survival rates. For the teens at the summit, prevention comes down to open conversation and making Narcan as common as any household product. Kahn said a lot of people have the stereotype that Narcan is only for responders and EMS, but people have to think about it as a household product, just like Benadryl.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September citing low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. He explained that the decision reflects standard airline industry practices, noting that air carriers adjust their routes based on demand.

Not everyone agrees the route had sufficient time to establish itself. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He emphasized the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying "It's easy. It's close." The Boston route from Vero Beach continues to perform well according to Dambeck, who said it is seeing great demand. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time.

Regarding the possibility of the JFK route returning in the future, Dambeck said JetBlue will continue to evaluate the market. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. He noted that air carriers regularly fluctuate their routes based on demand, characterizing such adjustments as normal business operations in the airline industry.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs low-altitude Blue Angels flyover in Pensacola as Navy halts safety review
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth voiced support for a fighter jet that flew so low over a Pensacola beach Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears.
cards.body:
Video spreading widely on social media shows a jet from the Navy's demonstration squadron, the Blue Angels, flying so low over a crowded beach in Pensacola on Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears. The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly afterward that it was conducting a thorough safety review. Then on Thursday morning, a host of Trump administration officials heaped praise on the maneuver. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on his personal X account that the flyovers will continue until morale improves. The Pentagon's top spokesman, Sean Parnell, wrote "Carry on Patriots" on social media alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above the heads of beachgoers. The White House tweeted a cartoon showing people on a beach taking photos of a Blue Angels jet, with the words "Freedom" and "It's okay to love America."

It is at least the third time that Hegseth and others have voiced support for military aviators performing maneuvers that have drawn public scrutiny and military investigations. In two prior cases, Hegseth's remarks led to the end of the safety investigations. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump administration political appointee, said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. Cao's post said Thursday that the Blue Angels conducted a flight debrief. Navy officials would not say if that debrief, typically a routine occurrence after every flight, was the thorough safety review the Navy said it would conduct the day prior. Jeff Guzzetti, an aviation safety consultant who used to investigate crashes for both the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration, said it is shocking that the top leaders of the military would excuse this type of reckless behavior. Florida beachgoer Alexandra Belcher, 34, called the Blue Angels flyover a once-in-a-lifetime experience and said it was such a blessing to be able to witness that with everybody she was with.

hero.headline: West Palm Beach company launches hurricane evacuation flight service for $1,250 membership
hero.teaser: A West Palm Beach company is offering Floridians a guaranteed seat on chartered flights out of the state when a hurricane threatens for a $1,250 annual membership fee.
hero.body:
A West Palm Beach company is betting Floridians will pay $1,250 for a guaranteed seat on a chartered flight out of the state when a hurricane threatens. Priority Evac founder Jason Murgio said the membership-based service was born from personal experience watching people struggle to leave ahead of storms. "Priority Evac really came out of me personally watching people I know try to leave ahead of a storm," Murgio said. The plan offers members a seat on a chartered Airbus departing from the three major South Florida airports and three others on the West Coast, with all flights heading to Atlanta. A single membership covers evacuations for two storms per season.

Murgio said operations are led by a retired Air Force colonel who ran chief of operations duties at NORAD and NORTHCOM and has personally directed Florida hurricane evacuations. The service is designed to get members out before highways jam and airfares spike, two problems that routinely plague Florida evacuations. "The whole idea is the plan is already in place and before everyone else starts scrambling, you know that you have a route out," Murgio said.

The concept appears to be unlike anything travel experts have seen before. Clint Henderson, managing editor of news at The Points Guy travel website, said the company's credentials are promising, but questions remain until the service is tested by an actual storm. "That's why I'm extra cautious on something like this: they say they do have the planes and they do have some very serious people running this company, they say they have the planes prebooked, but we won't know till the rubber meets the road in an actual hurricane," Henderson said.

For families, the $1,250 per person cost can add up quickly. Murgio said there is already interest from people looking to join the hurricane evacuation service. The company is positioning itself as a solution to the chaos that often accompanies hurricane evacuations in Florida, when both road travel and commercial airline options become difficult or prohibitively expensive.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System hosts resource fair at Big Dog Ranch Rescue in Loxahatchee
cards.teaser: The West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System hosted a resource fair for veterans on Friday at Big Dog Ranch Rescue in Loxahatchee to connect veterans with healthcare enrollment and claims support.
cards.body:
The West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System hosted a resource fair for veterans on Friday at Big Dog Ranch Rescue in Loxahatchee. VA representatives assisted veterans with eligibility and health care enrollment, VA health care programs and claims support. A mobile medical unit was on site to address basic medical needs and allowed veterans to complete an initial primary care appointment on site and get into the VA system on the spot.

Richard "Buzz" Bryan, director of community relations and community engagement for the West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System, said the event is focused on reaching veterans who have not yet connected with VA services. "Who we're really trying to reach is our veterans that are not engaged, that are not enrolled in VA healthcare," Bryan said. Bryan, a combat veteran himself, said he did not utilize VA services for years and wants other veterans to learn from his experience. Big Dog Ranch Rescue provided information about its service dog training program, animal adoption opportunities and additional veteran-focused services. Veterans who were unable to attend can call the West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System at (561) 422-8387.

cards.headline: Epstein survivor shares story in WPTV documentary airing July 23
cards.teaser: A local survivor of Jeffrey Epstein's abuse is sharing her story as WPTV reflects on 20 years since the story first broke.
cards.body:
The survivor, who wishes to only go by her first name of Ashley, told WPTV Anchor Ashley Glass she first met Epstein when she was 15 years old. Glass asked Ashley if she thinks she will ever see justice. Ashley answered, "I want to be hopeful, but it's really hard because it seems like at least once a week we're getting slapped in the face by one of those revolving sticks that has like five hands on them. It's really hard to think that in my lifetime somebody is going to do the right thing."

Ashley details her quest for justice in the WPTV original documentary GROOMED: Surviving Epstein, on Thursday, July 23 at 7 p.m. The documentary comes as a team of journalists at WPTV is reflecting on 20 years since the tangled story of the late Jeffrey Epstein first broke.

cards.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program offers summer service projects for South Florida families
cards.teaser: The TLC Program at B'nai Torah Congregation in Boca Raton is connecting families with hands-on service projects this summer.
cards.body:
The program, led by Summer Faerman, is part of B'nai Torah Congregation's broader effort to connect people of all ages with mitzvah opportunities or meaningful good deeds. Organizers say the TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed and has helped make service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. Volunteers help with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors.

B'nai Torah Congregation describes the TLC Program as a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. The congregation says the program focuses on hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations, special needs and other community concerns. Participants can volunteer in a variety of ways, including making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers say the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major I-95 Ramp Closures Planned July 19-24
cards.teaser:
Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 17-24 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department
cards.body:
Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 17-24 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report highlights multiple full road and ramp closures expected to have the greatest impact on drivers.

## Major closures to know about

### Southbound I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

Motorists will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt-Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. FDOT has scheduled July 26-30 as contingency dates in case the work is delayed by weather or other unforeseen conditions.

### Martin Highway ramps closing at I-95

Two ramps serving Martin Highway at I-95 will close overnight from **Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to Martin Highway at Exit 110 will be closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Drivers will continue north to Becker Road at Exit 114, travel west on Becker Road and use southbound I-95 to return to the Martin Highway exit.

The northbound I-95 entrance ramp from Martin Highway will also be closed during the same hours. Motorists will be detoured east on Martin Highway, north on Newfield Parkway and west on Becker Road to reach the northbound I-95 entrance ramp.

FDOT said only one ramp closure will occur at a time.

### Orange Avenue exit closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

Drivers will be detoured to the eastbound Orange Avenue exit, north on Jenkins Road and west on Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are scheduled for July 26-30.

### Emergency repairs could cause major delays on I-95

Southbound I-95 between Kanner Highway and Bridge Road will have **two lanes closed beginning at 4 p.m. Monday, July 20, and Tuesday, July 21.** The lanes are scheduled to reopen by 5:30 a.m. each morning.

FDOT said the closures are needed to complete an emergency repair near mile marker 98. Drivers are encouraged to consider alternate routes because the early closure time could affect the evening commute.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads may close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several roads near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project. Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 20, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 24,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. Adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained throughout the work.

Detours will use nearby roads including SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and SW McDevitt Avenue. FDOT is also providing advance notice that SW Paar Drive between SW McIntosh Street and SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard may close from July 27-31.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Northbound and southbound I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line will continue to have two lanes closed overnight for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

U.S. 1 between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue may have two lanes closed intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times Monday through Friday for pavement widening and drainage work. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday for milling and resurfacing.

In Stuart, two westbound lanes on Monterey Road between Ocean Boulevard and Monterey Commons Boulevard may close from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday through Thursday.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during daytime and overnight hours.

SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard will have intermittent lane closures from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road will continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures as part of the widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions continue

Boaters traveling near the North Causeway Bridge in Fort Pierce could encounter partial or full channel closures as crews continue removing sections of the former drawbridge.

Partial channel restrictions may occur during daylight hours on weekdays through late 2026. At least 45 feet of the channel is expected to remain open during partial closures.

Intermittent full channel closures lasting up to six hours may occur through July for the removal of steel bascule bridge spans. Vessels requiring full channel access must provide the bridge tender with 120 minutes of advance notice.

The new North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, although nearby roads including U.S. 1, Old Dixie Highway, Juanita Avenue and Harbortown Drive may have lane restrictions.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

I-95 near the new Oslo Road interchange may have one or two lanes closed overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for roadway construction.

Drivers near Sebastian Inlet should expect intermittent lane and shoulder closures on A1A from July 20-31. Flaggers will direct traffic through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park remain closed during construction of the replacement bridge, although the park, boat ramp and portions of both parking areas remain open.

## Additional I-95 closures coming the following week

FDOT is also providing advance notice of several closures scheduled to begin Sunday, July 26. All four I-95 ramps at Midway Road are expected to close separately overnight through July 31 for paving. Only one ramp will close at a time.

Detours will use St. Lucie West Boulevard, U.S. 1 and nearby interstate exits. Additional ramp closures are also planned later at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway.

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Drivers should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through [Florida 511](https://fl511.com). Updated lane closure information is available through [FDOT District Four](https://www.fdot.gov/info/co/district4).

cards.headline: Target theft suspect stole over $2,700 through self-checkout scheme
cards.teaser: A suspect is accused of stealing more than $2,700 from Target using fraudulent self-checkout tactics.
cards.body:
A theft suspect faces charges for allegedly stealing more than $2,700 from Target through a self-checkout scheme. The suspect is accused of manipulating the self-checkout system to avoid paying for merchandise.

The theft occurred over multiple visits to the store. Investigators determined the suspect used the self-checkout lanes to ring up items at lower prices or avoid scanning them altogether.

The suspect was identified and arrested on theft charges. The case highlights ongoing retail theft issues at self-checkout stations.

cards.headline: U-Haul passenger arrested after tossing cigarette leads police to find cocaine in shoe
cards.teaser: A U-Haul passenger faces drug charges after police found cocaine hidden in a shoe following a littering stop.
cards.body:
A passenger in a U-Haul was arrested on drug charges after allegedly tossing a lit cigarette, which led police to discover cocaine hidden in a shoe. The traffic stop began when an officer observed the littering violation.

During the stop, police conducted a search that revealed cocaine concealed inside the passenger's shoe. The initial contact stemmed from the discarded cigarette.

The passenger was arrested and charged with drug possession. The U-Haul stop resulted in the drug discovery and subsequent arrest.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Murray Middle School demolition has begun in Martin County as part of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage from Hurricane Milton.
cards.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay.

Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine the district was able to add these on. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast seeks fosters during shelter renovation
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation.
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation. The construction will modernize the shelter, improve animal living spaces, enhance adoption areas, and create more comfortable and visible spaces to care for animals. In the meantime, the renovation presents significant challenges for the animals, who are being held in smaller spaces during the work.

Sarah Fisher of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said the animals are being affected by the sound of the construction. It's very loud and the sound being in a closed kennel can be very stressful for an animal, she said. About 50 animals are currently in foster care, but the shelter is hoping to get the remaining 67 animals housed on-site either fostered or adopted, with most of them being dogs. The shelter continues to receive animals daily and is on a mission to get them out as quickly as they come in.

hero.headline: Messi bathed Spain star Lamine Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot before World Cup final matchup
hero.teaser: Photos from a 2007 UNICEF charity calendar show teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal, who now faces Argentina in Sunday's World Cup final for Spain at age 19.
hero.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing a baby boy in a plastic bathtub in 2007 for a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. The infant was Lamine Yamal, whose mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate in the photo shoot. Yamal is now 19 years old and will face Messi's Argentina for Spain in Sunday's World Cup final in New Jersey. Messi is 20 years his senior. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble, and Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

Monfort, 58, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, said he had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with the World Cup final approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets, while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation. Monfort said his loyalty is split between Messi, whom he calls the best player of all time, and Yamal, who represents a new, diverse Spain with parents from Morocco and Equatorial Guinea.

cards.headline: Argentina defeats England 2-1 with late goals to advance to World Cup final against Spain
cards.teaser: Argentina rallied from a 1-0 deficit with goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals.
cards.body:
Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Argentina scored twice in the final moments to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday in Atlanta. Enzo Fernandez scored the equalizer in the 85th minute, and substitute Lautaro Martinez headed in the winner two minutes into stoppage time. Lionel Messi assisted on both goals, feeding Fernandez outside the box before sending in a cross for Martinez.

England captain Harry Kane scored the opening goal in the 55th minute through Anthony Gordon. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves as Argentina dominated possession late in the match. Alexis Mac Allister sent a header off the post before Argentina's comeback.

The defending champions will face European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team proved its collectiveness and brotherhood by fighting to the very end. England coach Thomas Tuchel said his team played with a feeling they had a lot to lose, while Argentina played with more risk and rhythm.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey with President Trump attending
cards.teaser: Federal agents and local law enforcement will implement the highest level of security for Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain in New Jersey, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation.
cards.body:
A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there's anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

cards.headline: Major League Baseball restricts dugout iPad use to prevent AI decision-making
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday night to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence to make in-game decisions.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night when the second half of the season started, restricting the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. In many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches, according to a June 11 memo from MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword. The memo was sent to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season was intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments, Sword wrote. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts qualify for Junior Olympics after national top 15 finish
cards.body:
Three young gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month, qualifying for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine competed as a team after advancing through states and regionals during what Head Coach Candice Lazuka described as a strong season that included local and travel competitions. The team came close to a perfect score at nationals, earning a 9.9. Lazuka said it's hard to get a perfect 10.

The three gymnasts each found their way to the sport through different paths. Rose-Daris said it wasn't really gymnastics but the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan was inspired by all the gymnasts she saw on YouTube and how amazing they are and how fun it looks. Rine said she loves it because she learns new things. Rose-Daris said competing in Iowa is going to be really fun because she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described the qualification as happy and exciting at the same time. Rine said she is focused on getting first place on floors heading into the Junior Olympics.

hero.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free program through August 10
hero.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo extended its Kids Free promotion through August 10, allowing up to four children ages 3 to 12 to receive free admission with one adult ticket.
hero.body:
Palm Beach Zoo extended its popular Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, according to zoo officials. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, shared the updates during WPTV's "Shining A Light" segment from the zoo Monday morning. Joiner said the extension is designed to help local families enjoy affordable outings during the hottest stretch of summer while still supporting the zoo's conservation mission. Zoo officials emphasized that families still receive the full zoo experience through the promotion, including access to exhibits, shaded walkways and animal encounters. The zoo is also encouraging visitors to stay cool with indoor spaces, shaded pathways and frozen treats available throughout the park.

The zoo's newest koala joey is officially a boy and now has a name: Bonza. Joiner said that's Aussie slang for "awesome" or "excellent" during the interview. Palm Beach Zoo also announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. The themed nights include "Paws & Santa Claus" in July, "Tails & Touchdowns" in August and "Decades After Dark" in September. The events will feature live entertainment, themed activities and performances from bands including Whiskey Six and Snapback. Palm Beach Zoo is located at 1301 Summit Blvd.

cards.headline: Downtown Delray Beach launches Wellness Pass with free fitness classes and spa discounts
cards.teaser: The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August with free fitness classes and wellness offers.
cards.body:
Downtown Delray Beach is offering a new Wellness Pass featuring free fitness classes, yoga sessions, spa discounts and wellness-focused offers across the city's downtown district. The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the mobile-exclusive pass for July and August. The pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses throughout Downtown Delray Beach.

The pass does not require an app download. Miller Physical Therapy is participating with wellness-related services and promotions. According to the DDA, the program is designed to help residents and visitors prioritize health and self-care this summer.

More information and a complete list of participating offers can be found on the DDA's website. The program arrives as wellness tourism and fitness-focused experiences continue to grow in popularity across South Florida.

cards.headline: Boca Raton synagogue offers summer volunteer program for South Florida families
cards.teaser: The TLC Program at B'nai Torah Congregation offers hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
cards.body:
Families looking for ways to give back this summer can take part in the TLC Program at B'nai Torah Congregation, where volunteers help with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. The program, led by Summer Faerman, is part of B'nai Torah Congregation's broader effort to connect people of all ages with mitzvah opportunities or meaningful good deeds. Organizers say the TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed and has helped make service a central part of synagogue life since 2012.

B'nai Torah Congregation describes the TLC Program as a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. The congregation says the program focuses on hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations, special needs and other community concerns. Participants can volunteer in a variety of ways, including making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers say the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

cards.headline: Delray Beach dance studio hosts Bridgerton masquerade gala July 24 for ninth anniversary
cards.teaser: Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach is celebrating nine years with a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala featuring themed decor and dancing.
cards.body:
Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, located at 247 SE Sixth Ave., is hosting a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala on July 24 to celebrate its ninth anniversary. The studio is owned by world champion dancers Mar Martinez and Clifton Sepulveda and has built a reputation for welcoming dancers of all experience levels, from beginners to competitive performers. The anniversary gala will feature themed décor, dancing and a celebration of the studio's growth over the past nine years.

The studio is launching a Summer Boot Camp series beginning July 18 and continuing every Saturday through August. According to Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, the classes are designed to help participants learn ballroom and Latin dance fundamentals in a fun, supportive environment. Another upcoming event is a DJ Latin Dance Night open to the public on July 31 from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. Martinez and Sepulveda are also preparing to teach a dance class at Florida Atlantic University beginning in August. More information about upcoming events and classes is available at FredAstaireDelrayBeach.com.

hero.headline: Florida fentanyl summit draws teens, grieving parents and DEA chief as overdose crisis takes center stage in Orlando
hero.body:
Teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country joined grieving parents and federal law enforcement at the Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week, united by a shared mission to stop fentanyl before it kills more Americans. The summit drew students who traveled from around the country to learn about the resurgence of fentanyl so they can return home with a message about one of the country's deadliest drug threats. Hannah Kahn, 18, explained that a relative addicted to methamphetamine encouraged her to prevent similar destruction in others' lives. Jasmine Figueroa, 19, told adults that drug education should not be a taboo topic, saying young people will get educated one way or another and parents should be the first to tell them the truth about drugs.

This year's summit welcomed the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration as a partner. DEA Administrator Terrance Cole spent time with victim families and said the poison is being manufactured and distributed out of Mexico by the Mexican cartels. Cole said the president has designated the Mexican cartels as foreign terrorists, which opens different avenues for the DEA to target them. The students, who are members of their community anti-drug coalitions, said fentanyl spreads because it is often laced in other drugs and young people may not recognize the danger. Kahn said people are not seeking out fentanyl necessarily, but it is just within other drugs.

For parents who have lost children, the summit is deeply personal. Mari Rodriguez's daughter, Imam, died of fentanyl poisoning in 2023 after she made the mistake of buying a Percocet pill that had fentanyl in it. Rodriguez said every day she has to live with what she didn't know and questions why she gave her some space. She said the fight against fentanyl in the U.S. should have started in 2009, when the first fentanyl was found on streets, because the people behind it are not stopping. A DEA chemist recently told reporters that one sample turned out to be 16 percent fentanyl, which is high.

While deaths from the synthetic opioid are down, tracking how widespread fentanyl has become is nearly impossible in part because of Narcan, an over-the-counter nasal spray that is increasing survival rates. For the teens at the summit, prevention comes down to open conversation and making Narcan as common as any household product. Kahn said a lot of people have the stereotype that Narcan is only for responders and EMS, but people have to think about it as a household product, just like Benadryl.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs low-altitude Blue Angels flyover in Pensacola as Navy halts safety review
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth voiced support for a fighter jet that flew so low over a Pensacola beach Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears.
cards.body:
Video spreading widely on social media shows a jet from the Navy's demonstration squadron, the Blue Angels, flying so low over a crowded beach in Pensacola on Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears. The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly afterward that it was conducting a thorough safety review. Then on Thursday morning, a host of Trump administration officials heaped praise on the maneuver. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on his personal X account that the flyovers will continue until morale improves. The Pentagon's top spokesman, Sean Parnell, wrote "Carry on Patriots" on social media alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above the heads of beachgoers. The White House tweeted a cartoon showing people on a beach taking photos of a Blue Angels jet, with the words "Freedom" and "It's okay to love America."

It is at least the third time that Hegseth and others have voiced support for military aviators performing maneuvers that have drawn public scrutiny and military investigations. In two prior cases, Hegseth's remarks led to the end of the safety investigations. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump administration political appointee, said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. Cao's post said Thursday that the Blue Angels conducted a flight debrief. Navy officials would not say if that debrief, typically a routine occurrence after every flight, was the thorough safety review the Navy said it would conduct the day prior. Jeff Guzzetti, an aviation safety consultant who used to investigate crashes for both the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration, said it is shocking that the top leaders of the military would excuse this type of reckless behavior. Florida beachgoer Alexandra Belcher, 34, called the Blue Angels flyover a once-in-a-lifetime experience and said it was such a blessing to be able to witness that with everybody she was with.

cards.headline: Florida lawmaker caught off guard by massive development push unleashed by new state law
cards.teaser: A Florida lawmaker said she was caught flat-footed by a massive development push unleashed by a new law.
cards.body: Krista Joseph said she did not know a massive wave of development was coming as a result of new legislation. The lawmaker was caught off guard by the development push that the new law unleashed across the state. Joseph's remarks suggest the law had unintended or unexpected consequences for development activity in Florida.

hero.headline: Murray Middle School demolition begins in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
hero.teaser: Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, starting a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage from Hurricane Milton.
hero.body:
Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the beginning of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage from Hurricane Milton. The demolition phase alone will cost $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not yet been finalized. Officials plan to fund the reconstruction through a combination of local capital improvement funds, sales tax revenue, and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students displaced from damaged classrooms are continuing their education in portable units while the construction work proceeds.

The project encompasses more than just repairing storm damage. According to Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, Murray Middle School was already scheduled for significant construction work before the hurricane struck. The planned improvements included a new administration area, a new media center, and a brand new art lab. When Hurricane Milton's tornadoes destroyed buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district incorporated reconstruction of those structures into the existing improvement plans. The comprehensive project will also include a complete overhaul of the school's parking lot.

Safety has been a priority as construction proceeds on the active campus. The school district has installed barriers around the work zone to prevent students from entering construction areas and to maintain a secure learning environment. These safety measures are designed to allow normal school operations to continue while extensive construction work takes place. District officials have emphasized that parents can be assured their children will remain safe during the construction period, with precautions in place to separate students from the work areas.

The Martin County School District aims to complete all renovations by December 2027. The extended timeline reflects the scope of work required to both repair the tornado damage and complete the previously scheduled facility improvements. By combining the storm recovery effort with already planned upgrades, the district is working to turn the challenges created by Hurricane Milton into an opportunity for comprehensive campus modernization. The rebuilt and renovated Murray Middle School is expected to serve students with improved facilities for years to come, transforming destruction into a chance for significant enhancement of the educational environment.

cards.headline: FDOT to Hold Public Workshops on Willoughby Boulevard Improvement Study
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Transportation will hold two public workshops to discuss proposed improvements along Willoughby Boulevard between Monterey Road and U.S. 1 in Martin Count
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Transportation will hold two public workshops to discuss proposed improvements along Willoughby Boulevard between Monterey Road and U.S. 1 in Martin County.

The meetings are part of a Project Development and Environment, or PD&E, study examining potential alternatives for the corridor. FDOT will offer the workshop in virtual and in-person formats, and each meeting will include a presentation followed by an opportunity for residents to ask questions and provide feedback.

## Virtual workshop scheduled for July 28

The virtual workshop will begin at **5:30 p.m. Tuesday, July 28.** Participants must register in advance at [https://tinyurl.com/Willoughby-APW](https://tinyurl.com/Willoughby-APW).

People who prefer to join by phone can call **1-469-423-0557** and enter access code 35124623#.

Registered participants will receive an email containing a link to join the meeting. Those attending from a mobile device will need the free Microsoft Teams application. FDOT recommends allowing enough time to log in before the presentation begins.

## In-person workshop scheduled for July 29

The in-person workshop will begin at **5:30 p.m. Wednesday, July 29,** at the 10th Street Community Center, 724 SE 10th Street, Stuart, FL 34994.

The meeting will use an open-house format. FDOT staff will be available to explain the proposed alternatives, answer questions and assist attendees.

Questions and comments will be addressed in the order they are received. If a question cannot be answered during the event, FDOT will provide a written response after the meeting. Residents may also submit questions or comments before the workshop by contacting the project manager.

## What the study will evaluate

A PD&E study is an early phase of the transportation planning process used to evaluate possible improvements and determine how a project could move forward.

The process typically considers traffic operations, roadway safety, environmental effects, community impacts, engineering needs and estimated costs. Feedback gathered during the workshops will help FDOT evaluate the proposed alternatives for Willoughby Boulevard.

## Accessibility accommodations available

Anyone requiring accommodations under the Americans with Disabilities Act should contact FDOT at least seven days before the meeting.

Accommodation requests may be directed to FDOT Project Manager Vanita Saini, P.E., at **954-777-4468** or [Vanita.Saini@dot.state.fl.us](mailto:Vanita.Saini@dot.state.fl.us). Written requests may be mailed to the Florida Department of Transportation, 3400 West Commercial Boulevard, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309.

People with hearing or speech impairments may contact the Florida Relay Service at 1-800-955-8771 for TDD service or 1-800-955-8770 for voice service.

For additional project information, contact Saini at 954-777-4468 or toll-free at 866-336-8435, extension 4468.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce woman wins $5 million on $20 scratch-off ticket
hero.body:
Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6, Florida Lottery officials announced Friday. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.

Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The store sold the ticket that turned a $20 purchase into a multimillion-dollar jackpot.

The $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH game has overall odds of winning of 1-in-2.90. The chance of winning the $5 million top prize in this game is 1-in-4,018,135.

Florida Lottery officials released the information Friday afternoon about the April prize claim. Duran received her payment after choosing the lump-sum option rather than annuity payments over time.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. The decision reflects how the airline industry operates, with air carriers fluctuating based on demand.

Dambeck said the airline just was not seeing what they were hoping for with the route. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. Ahern said he thinks if the airline had hung in there, it would have worked and built up pretty good. He said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat, noting that it is easy and close.

Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said that route is performing well, with Boston seeing great demand. The contrast between the two routes highlights how different markets can perform dramatically differently even from the same regional airport. While the Boston service continues to attract passengers, the JFK route struggled to maintain the ridership levels JetBlue needed to justify continuing the service.

As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed. The airline will evaluate continuously, so just because the route is gone now does not mean it will never come back. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.
